consequence.statement: Certificates signed by CA and SelfSigned issuers with RSA keys 3072 bits and above will now use SHA-384 or SHA-512 hash algorithms; downstream systems consuming these certificates must support these hash algorithms to avoid compatibility issues.
consequence.remediation: Verify that all systems relying on certificates from CA and SelfSigned issuers support SHA-384 and SHA-512 hash algorithms, especially if using RSA keys 3072 bits or larger.

original.statement: The CA and SelfSigned issuers now use SHA-512 when signing with RSA keys 4096 bits and above, and SHA-384 when signing with RSA keys 3072 bits and above.

decision.reason: [ev-53fb690413df] says the CA and SelfSigned issuers now sign with SHA-384 for RSA keys of 3072 bits and above and SHA-512 for 4096 bits and above, and tells operators to "check that your systems support the new hash algorithms". It does not say that issuance fails, that anything is rejected or that a migration is required. Signing keeps working with a different hash, and any breakage depends on whether downstream systems support it. That makes this a behavior-change (review), and the proposed statement, remediation and medium severity match the note.
